title: [Epic] Phase 10: Determinism & Reproducibility
description:
## Background
The MLSys P0 gate requires every stochastic experiment to state temperature, sample count, and statistical method. Sample count and stats PASS. TEMPERATURE FAILS.

## Goals
- Every experiment's decoding config is stated in the paper and set in the code
- Model snapshots are pinned so results can be re-derived

## Non-Goals
- Re-running everything at temp=0. That is not obviously the right call (see below).

## Considerations
This does NOT invalidate the results: paired McNemar on identical tasks absorbs run-to-run noise, and single-trial is disclosed. The failure is OMISSION.
CRITICAL INSIGHT: temp=0 does NOT buy reproducibility here - the authors' own artifact shows a 32%->100% baseline swing at temp=0 from a model-snapshot drift. The real missing control is MODEL PINNING. Do not 'fix' this by re-running at temp=0 and assuming determinism.
Source: MNT-101..104

title: P10-1: Disclose temperature for every experiment (headline matrices run at 1.0)
description:
## What
State the decoding config for every experiment in main.tex, and reconcile with what the code sets.

## Why
bench/agents/long_context_qa.py (ContextCompress, n=300) and gaia_router.py (ModelDowngrade, n=127) - THE TWO HEADLINE ISOLATION MATRICES - plus the shared _runtime.py call_llm helper contain ZERO occurrences of 'temperature'. They run at the OpenAI default of 1.0. So do batch_classifier (CacheHit) and the anthropic/hf/concurrent variants.
There is NO global determinism/seed policy statement anywhere in main.tex. Temperature is stated only for the 3 experiments that actually set it.
A reader meets the paper's determinism framing and reasonably assumes it covers the headline results. It does not.

## How
Cheapest honest fix: add a decoding-policy paragraph stating exactly which experiments run at temp=0 and which at the provider default, and note that pairing (McNemar on identical tasks) absorbs decoding noise. Do NOT silently re-run - see P10-3 first.

## Risks
Reviewers WILL ask about temperature. Better to state it than be asked.

## Success
Every experiment's temperature is stated; no reader can infer determinism where there is none.
Findings: MNT-101, MNT-102

title: P10-2: Pin model snapshots - the actual missing control
description:
## What
Pin explicit model snapshots (e.g. gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18) rather than floating aliases, across bench agents and repro scripts.

## Why
THIS IS THE REAL BUG, not temperature. planner_ablation.summary.txt documents: 'Re-runs at temperature=0 yield 100% baseline accuracy - the model's behavior on this fixture at temp=0 has drifted since the original ablation.' composition_qa.py has set temperature=0 SINCE ITS FIRST COMMIT. So the same fixture, same model alias, same temp=0 moved from 32% to 100% baseline accuracy - a 68pp swing with decoding stochasticity nominally eliminated. The drift is server-side (snapshot change).
Corroborated on a SECOND provider: DATA_MANIFEST:55 blames a significant autogen result on a 'LLaMA temperature variance artifact' - on an agent that DOES set temp=0.

## Success
Every paper result names the exact model snapshot it ran against. Future re-runs are comparable.
Findings: MNT-103, MNT-104

title: P10-3: Decide what to do about tab:planner-ablation - authors say it no longer reproduces
description:
## What
AUTHOR DECISION REQUIRED. The paper's planner ablation (tab:planner-ablation, +18pp, p=0.0039) rests on a 32% shared baseline that the authors' own summary txt says no longer replicates - re-runs now yield 100% baseline.

## Why
If baseline is now 100%, '+18pp' is not merely unverifiable - it is arithmetically impossible to recover. An artifact reviewer who re-runs it gets a different world.
Note DATA_MANIFEST:70-73 already files the dropped V2-CC+PD row under 'UNRECOVERABLE (no artifacts, cannot reproduce without re-run)'.

## Options
(a) Re-run against a PINNED snapshot and report the new numbers (needs P10-2 first)
(b) Keep the result and add an explicit non-reproducibility caveat naming the snapshot drift
(c) Cut the table
Recommend (a) - the fixture is small (n=50) and it is the honest fix.

## Risks
This is a paper table with a significant p-value. Do not quietly leave it.

## Success
The table either reproduces against a pinned snapshot, or carries an honest caveat, or is gone.
Findings: MNT-103

title: V5: Measure TRUE end-to-end optimizer overhead (the paper's number excludes the audit write)
description:
## What
Measure real per-call overhead INCLUDING write_plan_audit. Compare against the paper's p50=76us / 120us.

## Why
crates/agentc-profiler/src/lib.rs:766 stops the stopwatch immediately after rust_plan and BEFORE write_plan_audit - which re-parses BOTH JSON payloads from scratch (two full deserializations of the entire prompt) and then does a synchronous SQLite INSERT into a DB opened with NO PRAGMAs (journal_mode=DELETE + synchronous=FULL) = an fsync per plan call.
main.tex reports 76us/120us and calls overhead 'sub-millisecond'; the conclusion repeats it. An fsync is typically 0.1-1ms on SSD - potentially LARGER than the entire measured overhead.
MAGNITUDE IS UNKNOWN. This is a blind spot, not yet a proven error.

## How
Instrument the full optimize_plan FFI call end to end. Also measure with WAL enabled (see P8 C1) to see how much of it is the fsync.

## Success
A real end-to-end number. If it exceeds 1ms, the paper's 'sub-millisecond' claim and fig:overhead must change.
Findings: MNT-072, MNT-073

title: [Epic] Phase 11: Test Coverage of Paper Claims
description:
## Background
Safe abstention and warmup gating are genuinely well tested (all 9 rules have real negative tests). The two claims the paper leans HARDEST on are not.

## Goals
- Every mechanism the paper claims is covered by a test that would FAIL if the mechanism were removed
- Delete or fix tests that provide false assurance

## Non-Goals
- Chasing a coverage percentage

## Considerations
The recurring anti-pattern: tests that pass whether or not the feature works. fail_open.rs reimplements catch_unwind in the test body; rules_integration.rs's self-labelled 'V2 paper gate' accepts BOTH Composed AND Rewritten; context_compress.rs:356 nests all assertions inside 'if let Some(p)' so it passes vacuously; tests/test_shadow.py tests a module with no production caller.
Source: MNT-105..110

title: P11-1: The guard's disable gate is tested for 1 rule out of 9
description:
## What
planner.rs:240 - 'if self.budget.is_disabled(..) { continue; }' - is the ONLY thing that disables ContextCompress, StateDrop, OutputBudget, PromptDedup, StructuredTruncation, DeadOutputTruncation, CacheHit, and ParallelBranch. It has NO TEST.

## Why
The accuracy guard is the PAPER'S HEADLINE CONTRIBUTION. Budget's unit tests are good (auto_disable_after_five_consecutive_breaches, cooldown, streak reset) but they test Budget IN ISOLATION. The wiring that makes it do anything is untested. ModelDowngrade self-defends in its own applies() so it is covered; the other 8 rules depend solely on planner.rs:240.
DELETING planner.rs:240-242 WOULD FAIL NO TEST. Grepping crates/agentc-optimizer/tests/ for 'disable' returns zero hits.

## Success
A test that breaches the budget for a non-MD rule and asserts the rule stops firing. It must fail if planner.rs:240 is removed.
Findings: MNT-105

title: P11-2: The guard does not run on the native Anthropic path
description:
## What
maybe_shadow_record - the guard's entry point - is called from exactly ONE place: _patches/_openai.py:415. _patches/_anthropic.py never calls it.

## Why
A user on the native Anthropic SDK gets NO accuracy guard and no warning.
SCOPE - IMPORTANT: this does NOT invalidate the paper's Claude Haiku cross-model guard result. That experiment routed Claude through the OpenAI-COMPATIBLE endpoint (BENCH_OPENAI_BASE_URL), so it exercised the OpenAI patch. The paper stands. The SHIPPED PRODUCT is what is broken.

## Success
Anthropic path calls maybe_shadow_record, or the limitation is documented.
Findings: MNT-106

title: P11-3: The Python->Rust guard loop is exercised by zero tests
description:
## What
The production chain is: maybe_shadow_record (_optimizer_glue.py:591) -> record_divergence (_optimizer.py:104) -> optimize_record_divergence (profiler/lib.rs:909) -> budget.record_sample -> budget.is_disabled -> planner.rs:240.
Tests cover the MIDDLE LINK ONLY (Budget in isolation). Both ends are untested.

## Why
- maybe_shadow_record has NO test references anywhere
- record_divergence is called only by bench/guard_overhead_bench.py (a benchmark, not a test)
- optimize_record_divergence is called by no test - AND cargo test EXCLUDES its crate (agentc-profiler)
- the AGENTC_SHADOW_DIVERGENCE_BUDGET override is untested

## Success
One end-to-end test that drives a real divergence through the FFI and asserts the rule gets disabled.
Findings: MNT-107

title: P11-4: The composition orthogonality gate has no test that reaches it
description:
## What
composition.rs:108-114 (the driver_conflict check) is unreachable by any existing test. Every test short-circuits at the EXPLICIT_SAFE / EXPLICIT_UNSAFE tables first (composition.rs:101-106 'continue's before :108 runs).

## Why
All three InputTokens pairs among (ContextCompress, PromptDedup, StateDrop) sit in one of the two explicit tables. The genuinely untested same-driver pairs are (OutputBudget, DeadOutputTruncation) - both OutputTokens - and (StructuredTruncation, PromptDedup/StateDrop).
DELETING composition.rs:108-114 WOULD FAIL NO TEST. The CompositionPlanner is the V2 contribution.

## Success
A test using a same-driver pair that is in NEITHER explicit table, asserting they do not compose.
Findings: MNT-108

title: P11-5: Delete or fix the four false-assurance tests
description:
## What
Tests that pass whether or not the feature works:
1. rules_integration.rs:432-501 'context_compress_and_output_budget_compose' - SELF-LABELLED 'V2 paper gate' - accepts BOTH Plan::Composed AND Plan::Rewritten (:495-498). If composition breaks entirely and only one rule fires, it still passes. The paper's composition claim is guarded by a test that passes either way.
2. context_compress.rs:356-380 - all assertions nested in 'if let Some(p) = prop { if let Plan::Rewritten {..} }'. If the rule returns None, ZERO assertions execute and it passes vacuously. The comment admits it: 'Either is acceptable.'
3. tests/test_shadow.py (whole file) - tests DEAD CODE. python/agentc/_shadow.py has NO production caller; its only importer is the test. 6 tests / 16 asserts create the appearance of shadow coverage while the REAL shadow path is untested. Most misleading file in the suite.
4. fail_open.rs:120-141 - see P7-5.

## Why
A test that cannot fail is worse than no test: it converts an unknown into a false 'covered'.

## Success
Each either fails when the feature is removed, or is deleted.
Findings: MNT-109

title: P11-6: CI silently skips the CLI tests and both provider-patch test groups
description:
## What
- tests/cli/test_cache_subcommands.py:32 skips if target/debug/agentc is missing. CI's python job NEVER runs cargo build -p agentc-cli, so the binary never exists -> the ENTIRE file (246 lines, 33 asserts) is skipped on EVERY CI run, silently.
- tests/test_anthropic_patch.py:469,482 and test_openai_patch.py:342 use importorskip. CI runs 'pip install -e .[dev]', and dev is only pytest/pytest-asyncio/mypy - anthropic and openai are SEPARATE extras, never installed. Both groups skip silently.
- cargo test --workspace --exclude agentc-profiler excludes the crate containing EVERY optimizer FFI binding, including the guard's entry point.

## Why
CI reports green while never executing the CLI, either provider patch, or any FFI binding.

## Success
CI builds the CLI binary and installs the provider extras. Skipped tests are reported loudly, not silently.
Findings: MNT-110

title: P11-7: wiring.rs has zero tests - and it reads the ablation knob the paper depends on
description:
## What
crates/agentc-optimizer/src/wiring.rs (273 LOC) has NO tests. build_optimizer (:163) is the sole production assembly point: it warms the budget from DB (:176), registers all 9 rules, and reads AGENTC_ENABLED_RULES (:205) - THE ABLATION KNOB EVERY PER-RULE SWEEP IN THE PAPER DEPENDS ON - plus AGENTC_PROVIDER (:136).

## Why
If AGENTC_ENABLED_RULES silently mis-parses, every ablation config in the paper is wrong and nothing would catch it.

## Success
A test asserting AGENTC_ENABLED_RULES actually gates the registered rule set.
Findings: MNT-111
close_reason: Diagnostic CLEAN: AGENTC_ENABLED_RULES unused by any experiment; real mechanism is 'optimize disable', and all 9 bench rule names match the runtime exactly. Ablation configs are sound. Latent typo-acceptance filed as P11-7b.

title: [Epic] Phase 12: Bench Harness Correctness & Consolidation
description:
## Background
25 run_*.py drivers, 6,992 LOC, ~85% boilerplate. The copy-paste drifted, and the drift changed numbers in the paper.

## Goals
- One parameterized driver + a config table. One fire-count query. One reset.
- Fix the fire-count predicates that undercount composed plans

## Non-Goals
- Re-running experiments whose SAVINGS numbers are unaffected (they are - savings come from traces.db, not the audit predicate)

## Considerations
BLAST RADIUS: cost/token savings are CLEAN. Only FIRE COUNTS are wrong, and only in multi-rule configs (*-only rows cannot compose, so they are correct).
run_guard_eval.py is already the right shape (fully env-parameterized) - generalize it.
Source: MNT-112..119

title: P12-1: Fire-count predicate misses composed plans - Tables 5/6/7/13 undercount
description:
## What
13 of 25 drivers query the audit DB with plan_kind='rewritten' ONLY. A composed plan is written as plan_kind='composed' with rule = ONLY THE FIRST RULE (crates/agentc-profiler/src/lib.rs:820-823). AGENTC_COMPOSE=1 is the default in every driver.

## Why - PROOF IS IN COMMITTED DATA
bench/paper_results/autogen_bridge_warmup_n200.csv:
  all-on:              sd_fire=0    cc_fire=396
  ContextCompress-off: sd_fire=197  cc_fire=0
  StateDrop-only:      sd_fire=197  cc_fire=0
StateDrop did NOT stop firing under all-on. Its fires were absorbed into composed rows attributed to CC. The same agent under run_autogen_warmup_n300.py (which DOES include 'composed') reports all-on sd=260.
4 drivers get it right: IN ('rewritten','composed'). 13 do not. Tables 5/6/7/13 come from the undercounting group.

## BLAST RADIUS (important - do not overcorrect)
Cost and input-token savings are UNAFFECTED - they come from traces.db, not the audit predicate. Only FIRE COUNTS are wrong, and only in multi-rule configs. Single-rule (*-only) rows cannot compose, so they are correct.

## Success
One shared fire-count query: plan_kind IN ('rewritten','composed','cached','parallel'), counting cached/parallel by plan_kind since rule is NULL for them. Recompute affected fire counts from committed audit DBs if retained; otherwise re-run only the fire-count cells.
Findings: MNT-112

title: P12-2: CacheHit fire counts are structurally impossible - the manifest reports CC's number
description:
## What
crates/agentc-profiler/src/lib.rs:809: 'Plan::Cached { .. } => (PlanKind::Cached, None, None)' - a cached plan logs rule = NULL. So WHERE rule='CacheHit' returns 0 in EVERY driver, BY CONSTRUCTION.

## Why
DATA_MANIFEST.txt:53 claims 'CacheHit fires 396/400 (98%)'. But 396 is exactly the cc_fire_count (ContextCompress) column of autogen_bridge_warmup_n200.csv for the all-on row. The manifest took ContextCompress's fire count and labelled it CacheHit.
The SAME bug structurally hides ParallelBranch (plan_kind='parallel', rule=NULL). This EXPLAINS MNT-058: PB may well have been firing all along and nothing could ever have counted it.

## Success
Count cached/parallel plans by plan_kind, not by rule. Correct the manifest. Re-examine every CacheHit and ParallelBranch claim.
Findings: MNT-113, MNT-058

title: P12-3: Two drivers never reset optimizer_audit.db - warmup fires leak into measurement
description:
## What
run_md_cc_orthogonality_warmup.py:264-270 and run_cc_sd_subadditivity_warmup.py:254-260 delete traces.db + traces.db.lock but NOT optimizer_audit.db. Every other warmup driver deletes all three.

## Why
Their fire counts therefore sum W=30 warmup fires + N measurement fires. These two drivers are the sources for sec 6.4 (MD+CC orthogonality) and Table 13 (CC+SD).
Cost/token columns are CLEAN (they come from traces.db, which IS deleted). Only fire counts are contaminated.
This is the SAME CLASS as the original contamination that produced planner_ablation_contaminated_original.csv - state leaking between phases.

## Success
One shared _reset_between_phases that deletes all three DBs. Recompute the affected fire counts.
Findings: MNT-114

title: P12-4: Warmup W is not uniform - the guard sweeps run with NO warmup at all
description:
## What
DATA_MANIFEST asserts a uniformly warmup-corrected harness. It is not.
  W=30: 12 drivers
  W=20: run_guard_eval.py, run_analyst_sd_generalization.py
  W=0 : run_guard_sweep.py:59 sets GE_W='0'; repro/guard_frontier.sh:18 and repro/crossmodel_selectivity.sh:27 export GE_W='0'
  none: run_planner_ablation_rerun.py (TABLE 14 SOURCE), run_md_cc_orthogonality_rerun.py, run_cc_sd_subadd_rerun.py, run_composition_check.py have NO warmup phase in the file

## Why
ALL ~60 committed gsweep_* / checkpoint_* / emb_ckpt_* CSVs are COLD-START, NO WARMUP. Those back tab:guard and tab:xmodel - the paper's HEADLINE.

## MITIGATING CONTEXT (verify before panicking)
specs/working/guard-frontier-findings.md already argues the guard results should be read on BEHAVIORAL axes (rule retention = fires/total, disabled yes/no, accuracy delta) which are sampling-rate independent, and explicitly says 'savings numbers are NOT usable from these cells'. If so, W=0 may be defensible for the behavioral claims.
BUT the paper DOES cite savings from these cells (CC stays enabled at 32.4-37.6%). That is the exposure. Resolve it.

## Success
W is an explicit column in every result CSV. The paper states the warmup config per experiment. The 32.4-37.6% guard savings claim is either re-derived from a warmed run or explicitly caveated.
Findings: MNT-115

title: P12-5: Composition results are measured on different tasks than the rules they are compared against
description:
## What
The warmup family sets BENCH_TASK_OFFSET=0 for BOTH phases (warmup subset of measurement - 'Option A'). But md_cc_orthogonality_warmup and cc_sd_subadditivity_warmup measure at offset=W (DISJOINT windows).

## Why
So the composition results (sec 6.4, Table 13) are measured on a different task window than the single-rule results they are compared against. That is not a like-for-like comparison.

## Success
One task-window policy, stated in the paper.
Findings: MNT-116

title: P12-6: Consolidate 25 drivers into one parameterized driver (~4,000 of 6,992 LOC removable)
description:
## What
25 run_*.py, 6,992 LOC, ~85% boilerplate. 11 form a near-clone 'warmup family' (mean pairwise identical-line ratio 80%, peak 89%).
Verbatim-duplicated helpers: _load_env (20/25 files), _binom_pmf + mcnemar_exact (17/25), _run_phase (14/25), _append_row (14/25), _reset_between_phases (12/25).

## How
run_guard_eval.py is ALREADY the right shape - fully env-parameterized (GE_AGENT, GE_W, GE_N, GE_TAG, GE_FIXTURE). Generalize into bench/run_ablation.py + an EXPERIMENTS table:
  Experiment(tag, agent, W, N, ceiling, configs, fire_rules, fixture, task_window='overlap'|'disjoint')
with ONE shared _run_phase / _reset_between_phases (all three DBs) / mcnemar_exact / CSV writer, and ONE fire-count query.

## Why this is not cosmetic
That single consolidation kills P12-1, P12-2, P12-3 and P12-7 at once, and makes W an explicit column so P12-4 becomes visible instead of buried.

## Success
~4,000 LOC removed. One driver. Divergence becomes structurally impossible.
Findings: MNT-118, MNT-083

title: P12-7: Column unit collision + dead bench agents
description:
## What
- run_guard_eval.py:58 emits 'cost_savings_pct' (a percentage) in the SAME schema slot where 10 other drivers emit 'cost_savings_mUSD' (millidollars). Same position, different unit.
- Dead agents (zero references repo-wide): parallel_research.py, adaptive_router.py, batch_classifier.py
- Runners producing no committed CSV: run_hotpot_ablation.py, run_oracle_baseline.py (both default --out bench/results/*.csv; that directory does not exist)
- run_sd_precondition_warmup.py:89 defines _reset_between_phases and never calls it (dead)
- run_lcqa_warmup.py uses sys.executable; run_lcqa_warmup_n300.py hardcodes .venv/bin/python

## Success
One unit per column name. Dead agents archived or wired to a runner.
Findings: MNT-117, MNT-119

title: [Epic] Phase 13: Silent Failure (Python swallowed errors)
description:
## Background
A swallowed error in a BENCHMARKING runtime is uniquely dangerous: a silently-disabled optimizer looks EXACTLY like 'no savings'. The paper's numbers cannot tell the difference.

## Goals
- 'Agentc wanted to optimize and could not' must be a WARNING, always - never DEBUG
- No swallowed path can silently disable a rule or over-credit savings

## Non-Goals
- Removing broad catches. Catching broadly is CORRECT for a library that monkey-patches other people's SDKs. The bug is the LOG LEVEL and the corrupt-state continuations.

## Considerations
ROOT CAUSE, and the highest-leverage fix: it is a logging-level POLICY problem, not a logic problem. _executor.py already gets this right (WARNING on fallback). Every sibling path doing the SAME fallback logs at DEBUG - including the sync path the benchmarks actually use.
Source: MNT-120..126

title: P13-1: An attention failure silently disables ContextCompress
description:
## What
_optimizer_glue.py:233 (OpenAI) and :401 (Anthropic): 'except BaseException' around compute_attention_scores sets attn_scores=[]. The next statement is 'if attn_scores:' - false - so attention_scores, follow_on_tokens, and dead_attention_epsilon are NEVER written into parameters.extra. The Rust ContextCompress rule reads exactly those keys and no-ops without them.

## Why
ANY exception inside compute_attention_scores (a tokenizer edge case, a _native.read_trace_content hiccup, an IDF divide) silently converts ContextCompress from 'firing' to 'never fires'. The only trace is log.debug.
A benchmark run would report honest-looking ZERO SAVINGS for the headline compression rule, and nothing would indicate anything broke.

## Success
Log at WARNING. Emit a counter. A rule that CANNOT fire must be distinguishable from a rule that CHOSE not to fire.
Findings: MNT-120
close_reason: attention_failed now WARNING via log_degraded (openai+anthropic). Commit 5a5e9f4

title: P13-2: A trace-recommendation failure silently disables StateDrop/DeadOutput/PrefixAlign
description:
## What
_optimizer_glue.py:222 and :396: 'except BaseException' around trace_optimizer.get_recommendations skips injection of inferred_state_reads, output_is_dead_branch, and shared_prefix_messages. All three rules read those extra keys and no-op without them.

## Why
Same mechanism as P13-1. DEBUG only. Three rules silently stop firing.
Compounding: _openai.py:294 (trace_opt.record) and :333 (cache auto-seed) are also swallowed at DEBUG - starving the two systems that FEED these rules. No record -> get_recommendations stays empty forever. No cache seed -> CacheHitRule never has anything to hit.

## Success
WARNING + counter.
Findings: MNT-121
close_reason: trace-rec + record + cache-seed failures now WARNING via log_degraded. Commit 5a5e9f4

title: P13-3: A failed rewrite is logged at DEBUG on the sync path (WARNING on async)
description:
## What
_optimizer_glue.py:659 (dispatch_sync): run_mutated raises -> log.debug -> run_original().
_executor.py:66 (async): the IDENTICAL event -> log.WARNING ('retrying original call once').
The sync path is the one the benchmarks use.

## Why
A systematically broken mutation (bad downgrade model name, malformed rewritten Call) reverts to the original on EVERY SINGLE CALL and reports 0% savings with no visible signal anywhere.

## Success
Sync path logs at WARNING, matching the async path.
Findings: MNT-122
close_reason: sync failed-rewrite fallback now WARNING (matches async). Commit 5a5e9f4

title: P13-4: OVER-reporting - a cached-decode failure returns None to the app while booking full savings
description:
## What
_openai.py:402: _decode_cached_openai catches internally and RETURNS None rather than raising. So dispatch_sync's except at _optimizer_glue.py:651 never fires, the fallback to run_original() is DEFEATED, and dispatch_sync returns None as the response.

## Why
The application receives None instead of a completion, AND the run books a cache hit with full savings credited. This corrupts in the OVER-reporting direction - the opposite of P13-1/2/3.

## Success
Raise, so the existing fallback works. Add a test.
Findings: MNT-123
close_reason: cached None/failed decode falls back to real call (sync+async); no None-to-app. +tests. Commit 5a5e9f4

title: P13-5: A swallowed getattr can auto-disable a working rule mid-run
description:
## What
_optimizer_glue.py:508: 'except BaseException' around _response_output_text returns ''. Then _text_divergence('', real_text) -> 1.0 (maximum divergence). That feeds record_divergence, and after BREACH_STREAK samples the Rust accuracy budget AUTO-DISABLES the rule for that call site.

## Why
A swallowed attribute error silently switches a WORKING rule off mid-run - and the guard's audit trail will show it as a legitimate divergence breach. This is the guard being fed a lie.

## Success
Distinguish 'could not read the response' from 'the response diverged'. Never feed an extraction failure into the divergence metric.
Findings: MNT-124
close_reason: _response_output_text returns None on failure; shadow sample skipped, not fabricated. Commit 5a5e9f4

title: P13-6: Any @agentc.trace function that raises is executed TWICE
description:
## What
_span.py:150 (async) / :172 (sync). _run_traced_sync:227 catches the USER's exception, logs it, and RE-RAISES (:232). The wrapper at :172 then catches that same re-raised user exception, cannot distinguish it from an Agentc-internal failure, and with fail_open=True (the DEFAULT) calls the user's function A SECOND TIME.

## Why
Duplicate LLM calls, duplicate token spend, and a span already emitted with status=ERROR for the first attempt. Logged at DEBUG.

## Success
Re-raise user exceptions without retrying. Distinguish user faults from Agentc faults. Test it.
Findings: MNT-125
close_reason: Traced fn tagged so user exceptions propagate (no double-exec); fail-open preserved. +test.

title: P13-7: Adopt a logging-level policy - 'wanted to optimize, could not' is always WARNING
description:
## What
Establish and enforce the invariant across python/agentc/.

## Why
THE ROOT CAUSE. ~130 except sites; the DANGEROUS ones nearly all log at DEBUG. Right now 'Agentc broke' is indistinguishable from 'Agentc correctly decided not to optimize' - and the paper's numbers cannot tell the difference either.
_executor.py already models the right behavior (WARNING on fallback, DEBUG reserved for genuinely uninteresting cases). _openai.py:730/732 also gets it right (patch failure -> logger.warning). Every other sibling path does not.

## How
Policy: any except that results in Agentc NOT doing something it intended to do logs at WARNING with a stable event name, and increments a counter surfaced by 'agentc optimize report'. Silent degradation becomes impossible.

## Also fix
- _memoize.py:116/139/147/159/172/237/265 - the cache silently degrades to a permanent 0% hit rate (every one at DEBUG)
- _writer.py:302/318/365 - dropped cache inserts and a failed merge_all_pending, at DEBUG
- _lifecycle.py:184 - install_all() failure means NO provenance tags -> ParallelBranch and StateDrop conservatively refuse to fire, silently
- _provenance_frameworks/langgraph.py:66 - falls through and forwards the UNWRAPPED node; provenance silently vanishes for that node
- _config.py:69 - a malformed config.toml silently reverts to defaults, discarding storage_path and fail_open

## Success
No DANGEROUS swallow logs below WARNING. A degraded run is loud.
Findings: MNT-126
close_reason: Degradation policy: log_degraded helper + counter + tests. Commit (foundation).

title: P8-1: Every cache lookup opens a new connection and re-runs the full DDL
description:
## What
agentc-memo/src/ffi.rs:279-286: SqliteCache::from_shared opens a NEW SQLite connection; cache.rs:93-94 then calls ensure_schema, executing the ENTIRE 9-statement DDL batch (3 CREATE TABLE, 5 CREATE INDEX, 1 CREATE VIEW). Then the actual SELECT. Then close. ALL WHILE HOLDING THE PROCESS-GLOBAL PROFILER MUTEX. insert() and maintenance() do it too.

## Why
Worst hot-path defect in the tree. The optimizer gets this right (one long-lived SqliteCache at wiring.rs:188); the memo FFI does not.

## Success
One long-lived connection. Schema ensured once.
Findings: MNT-074

title: P8-2: There is no working migration path - migrate_db cannot migrate
description:
## What
agentc-core/src/db.rs:336-350: 'let migrations_applied = 0;' is hardcoded; the body is a comment where migrations would go. It reads user_version and bumps it to 1 WITHOUT CREATING A SINGLE TABLE. Meanwhile create_db (db.rs:123-136) applies the schema only when version==0 and bails on any mismatch.

## Why
Bumping SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 BRICKS EVERY EXISTING traces.db (the profiler cannot start), and the documented escape hatch (agentc migrate) prints '0 migrations applied'.
Three DBs, three incompatible disciplines: only traces.db has versioning or PRAGMAs. cost_model.db and optimizer_audit.db have neither. The memoization tables live INSIDE traces.db but are not covered by its SCHEMA_VERSION, so its user_version is a lie about its own contents.

## Success
A real MIGRATIONS table plus a shared apply_migrations() used by all three DBs.
Findings: MNT-075

title: P8-3: The cross-process merge lock is defeatable - concurrent merges into traces.db
description:
## What
merge.rs:84-89 opens the lockfile with truncate(false) and NEVER WRITES to it, so its mtime is frozen at first creation. is_lockfile_stale (merge.rs:125-136) declares it stale at over 60s old.

## Why
After the first minute of an install's life the lockfile mtime is PERMANENTLY ancient. On any real contention: process B times out, is_lockfile_stale returns TRUE (always), B unlinks the file (merge.rs:62), creates a fresh one, and flocks a DIFFERENT INODE while A still holds the old one. BOTH PROCESSES THEN MERGE INTO traces.db CONCURRENTLY.
The staleness check keys on the lockfile mtime rather than the holder's liveness.

## Success
Liveness-based staleness (PID plus heartbeat), or touch the lockfile while held.
Findings: MNT-076

title: P8-4: optimizer_audit.db has no WAL - an fsync on every plan call
description:
## What
wiring.rs:179 opens optimizer_audit.db with a bare Connection::open - NO PRAGMAs at all. It therefore runs journal_mode=DELETE plus synchronous=FULL: a rollback journal created, written, FSYNCED, and unlinked PER PLAN CALL.
A comment at wiring.rs:185 asserts 'SQLite's WAL mode handles concurrent access.' WAL IS NEVER ENABLED.

## Why
Real per-call cost on the user's LLM call path, sitting OUTSIDE the stopwatch (see V5 / MNT-072). Fixing it may materially change the paper's overhead number.

## Success
WAL plus synchronous=NORMAL plus busy_timeout on all three DBs (consolidation item C1).
Findings: MNT-073, MNT-072

title: P8-5: The shadow/accuracy reporting surface is structurally dead
description:
## What
- rule_divergence is SELECTed at reporting.rs:162 and :414, but there is NO INSERT INTO rule_divergence ANYWHERE in the tree. Budget::record_sample folds divergence into a DashMap and never persists it; budget.rs:14-16 claims persistence is a snapshot on flush - no such flush exists.
- plan_audit.shadow_sampled is hardcoded FALSE and measured_savings_usd hardcoded None at the only production writer (profiler/lib.rs:834-837).

## Background

## Goals

## Non-Goals

title: P14-1: Reconcile the guard's '2% shadow cost' claim with the 100% operating point
description:
## What

## Why - MOST DAMAGING ITEM LEFT
run_guard_sweep.py:67 sets shadow='1'. bench/repro/guard_frontier.sh:10 states the reason: '(AGENTC_OPTIMIZE_SHADOW=1) SO DISABLES ACTUALLY TRIGGER' - i.e. at 2% the mechanism would not fire. Shadow calls invoke the UNPATCHED SDK method (_openai.py:367), so they emit NO SPAN - every guard run made a second real billed LLM call per rewrite, invisible to traces.db and to the cost column (which is /bin/zsh anyway, MNT-131).
So the guard was measured at 50x the sampling rate the abstract advertises, and the cost of that was never accounted.
This is also PRESUBMIT's existing P0 gate 'Guard sampling is truthful'.

## How
Either (a) run a rate sweep (2%, 5%, 10%, 100%) reporting disable latency, damage-before-disable, retained savings, and the doubled-call overhead at each; or (b) reframe the paper honestly: the behavioral result (metric selectivity, disable decisions) is sampling-rate-independent and holds at 100%; the '2%' is the PRODUCTION operating point, not the measured one. Say which is which.

## Success
No reader can believe the guard's damage-prevention was measured at 2% when it was measured at 100%.

## What

title: P14-3: Fix se_pp - single-arm binomial SE published as a paired-delta SE
description:
## What
15 drivers compute se = 100*sqrt(acc*(1-acc)/N) - the single-arm binomial SE - and print it as the uncertainty on the PAIRED delta (acc - baseline_acc).

## Why
A paired-delta SE depends on the DISCORDANT pairs (the McNemar b,c), not the marginal accuracy. The current value overstates delta uncertainty 2.3-2.7x (autogen n=300: published 2.5pp, true paired 0.94pp). It produces a visible contradiction: research_planner prints p=0.0117 (significant) beside +9.0 +/- 4.9, which spans zero at 2 SE.
Direction is CONSERVATIVE (overstates uncertainty), so no claim is inflated - but it is wrong and internally inconsistent, and a reviewer will catch the p-vs-SE contradiction.

## How
Compute the paired SE from the discordant counts (already available - the drivers compute BF/FB for McNemar). This is a recompute from committed per_task data - NO re-run needed. INERT/additive.

## Success
Every se_pp is the paired-delta SE. The p-value and the +/- no longer contradict.

title: P14-6: Disclose the multiple-comparisons surface and the accept-the-null problem
description:
## What
284 McNemar tests across committed CSVs, 26 p-values printed, 18 tables, ZERO multiplicity correction (no bonferroni/BH/holm/FDR anywhere). And the central SAFETY claim ACCEPTS THE NULL ('no significant degradation') without an equivalence test - no TOST, no power analysis, no minimum-detectable-effect anywhere.

## Why
A reviewer will note that with 284 tests, several 'significant' results are expected by chance, and that 'no significant degradation' from an underpowered test is not evidence of no degradation. The marginal p=0.044 powered check would not survive any correction.

## How
This is largely a WRITING fix (additive): state the number of tests, apply BH to the family where you claim significance, and reframe the safety claim as an equivalence/non-inferiority result (TOST) or explicitly as 'no evidence of degradation at this power' with the MDE stated. The Limitations section is already candid about underpowering - extend it.

## Success
The paper discloses its testing surface and does not treat a failure to reject as proof of the null.

title: [Epic] Phase 15: Durability, Guardrails & Paper-Writing Skills
description:
## Background
The audit found that this repo's failure mode is DRIFT: things were true once and silently stopped being true. The exploration waves designed the anti-drift layer (guardrails, project skills, biochem mechanisms) but NONE of it was filed as beads. This epic closes that gap.

## Goals
- Paper-writing/claims-integrity capability the repo lacks entirely
- Adapt proven skills (jsm library, biochem_pipeline) rather than reinvent
- Make good patterns durable: a claim cannot drift from its evidence, a test cannot pass when its feature is deleted

## Non-Goals
- A skill portfolio. biochem has 18 and admits none is verified. Build 3-4 that sit on the paths where drift is manufactured.

## Considerations
STYLE BAR: jsm skills (dunc-agent-skills / global ~/.claude/skills). Respect progressive disclosure (thin SKILL.md + deep references/), verification-first, machine-checkable outputs, MIT/distribution frontmatter.
Durability ladder: impossible-by-construction > CI > test > hook > skill > doc. A skill whose output nothing checks is advice.
Source: durability + guardrail + biochem exploration waves

title: P15-1: SELF-CREATE agentc-claim-evidence skill (the flagship)
description:
## What
A project skill that binds every number in main.tex to the committed CSV cell it came from, and a CI checker that fails on any unbacked or drifted number.

## Why
18 verified defects (MNT-040..057) are one defect: a number typed by hand into main.tex, never re-derived from its CSV. The abstract is falsified by its own data. No off-the-shelf skill covers this - it must be built.

## Adapt, do not invent
- jsm document-to-latex's 'round-trip compile-and-diff plus numeric preservation' IS this mechanism, aimed at conversion instead of claims. Borrow the numeric-preservation loop.
- biochem's watched_inputs digest: a claim declares its dependencies, they are hashed, and 'verified' auto-EXPIRES when they change. Cache invalidation applied to trust.
- biochem's deterministic projection: the doc IS the source rendered, so it cannot disagree.

## Design (from the durability wave)
CLAIMS.tsv or claims.yaml: claim_id | value | main.tex:label | csv | column | row_selector | recompute_expr | watched_inputs.
Checker asserts: CSV exists + sha matches; run_script exists; recompute re-derives the value; every table label resolves to a claim; a 'retracted' value may NOT appear in README/main.tex; coverage ratchet (every numeral in abstract/tables/captions is registered or on NOT_A_CLAIM, which may shrink never grow).
End state: generate claims.tex of \newcommands from CSVs so an unbacked number CANNOT COMPILE.

## Success
A skill + CI check. An unbacked paper number fails the build.
Findings: MNT-040..057, MNT-129

title: P15-3: SELF-CREATE agentc-test-honesty skill (the kill-the-mutant gate)
description:
## What
A skill enforcing: before claiming a test covers something, delete/mutate the exact production line it protects and paste the RED failure. Backed by cargo-mutants on a curated critical-lines list.

## Why
Four tests cannot fail (MNT-089, MNT-109 x3). The guard's disable gate - the paper's headline - is tested for 1 rule of 9 (MNT-105); the composition gate is unreachable (MNT-108). Deleting either line fails no test. This is the most AGENT-SHAPED failure: asked to 'add coverage', an agent writes green decoration.

## Design
critical-lines.toml: each entry is a line whose deletion MUST turn CI red (planner.rs:240 the disable gate; lib.rs:762 catch_unwind; composition.rs:108-114; wiring.rs:205 the ablation knob). Nightly: delete each span, assert the named test subset goes RED, restore. Skill emits a machine-checkable 'protects:' annotation so CI verifies it.

## Success
A surviving mutant on a critical line fails the build. Banned test shapes are rejected.
Findings: MNT-089, MNT-105, MNT-108, MNT-109, MNT-111

title: P15-5: ADOPT the 4 biochem durability mechanisms (~2.5 days)
description:
## What
The biochem drift-prevention layer, adapted. These OVERLAP with P15-1/P15-3 - implement whichever lands first and reference from the others.

## The four (from the biochem mining wave)
1. Executable claims manifest (= P15-1). Replace the prose DATA_MANIFEST.txt (which nothing reads) with a machine-checked claims.yaml.
2. Stale-reference pre-commit guard: path_redirects.yaml of old->new paths; any live file still naming a moved path FAILS the commit. Historical dirs exempted. ~80 lines, stdlib. Would have caught the dead script pointers (MNT-015).
3. CI that can fail: cargo BUILD not check; bare pytest not pytest tests/; a clean-runner smoke job; test modules enumerated by name so a skip is an error. (= P6 beads - cross-link.)
4. Evidence promotion boundary: paper_results/paper/ (hash-pinned) vs exploratory/. (= P15-4 + P5-1.)

## Why NOT more
biochem has 18 skills, a lifecycle state machine, ed25519 receipts, capability routing. SKIP all of it - proportionate to a research program with an indefinite horizon, overkill for 2 people / 14 weeks. Its own README admits no skill is verified.

## Success
A human-readable claim is never the source of truth. Drift is a build error.
Findings: MNT-015, MNT-025..028, biochem adoption

title: P15-7: SESSION-START reality check + evidence-immutability hook (nearly free, highest leverage)

1. PreToolUse deny on Edit/Write to bench/paper_results/**.csv - makes 'evidence is immutable' actually immutable for every agent, today, with no CI run.
2. SessionStart: emit the live rule count (from wiring.rs), crate count, and git log -5 into context, so an agent cannot start a session believing a stale fact.

## Why
MNT-024 (CLAUDE.md said 'no code exists') misinformed every agent session for 2 months. A doc an agent reads is the WEAKEST guardrail; a hook that fires is not. This converts the single most consequential invariant from a sentence into a tool call that cannot succeed. ~10 lines each.

## Success
No agent can edit a committed CSV or start on a stale fact.
Findings: MNT-024, MNT-127 (evidence immutability)

title: P15-8: Rewrite CLAUDE.md to contain no fact that can decay
description:

## Why
MNT-024: 'No implementation code exists yet' was true in March, became the worst defect in the repo by May, edited by no one. A file that asserts only invariants CANNOT become a lie - if an invariant goes false, that is a code bug, not doc rot. Kills MNT-024 and the 5/8/9 rule-count split by construction.
Include the authority ladder (paper > CSV > PRESUBMIT > README; when they disagree the README is the bug) and the [UNENFORCED] tagging convention so the doc's own weak spots are visible and countable.

## Success
CLAUDE.md states no fact that git can prove stale.
Findings: MNT-024, MNT-030, MNT-031

title: P15-2a: Reuse verify_numbers.py as a no-number-dropped gate for the template port - PLUS a positional diff

Every bead close records docs_impact + validation_evidence. Drift is caught at introduction, not by a future audit.

title: P0-FREEZE-b: Also freeze/reconcile the SECOND price table in _optimizer_glue.py
description:
## What
Extends P0-FREEZE (bd-3w1). The freeze hash-pinned data/pricing.json - but that is the WRONG surface for the cross-model claims.

## Why - RED-TEAM A2
The provider-generalization and tab:xmodel COST numbers (MNT-132) do NOT come from pricing.json. Non-OpenAI models are ABSENT from it (structural $0.00, MNT-131). Those published numbers are computed from a SECOND hardcoded table at _optimizer_glue.py:60-101, which:
  - DISAGREES with pricing.json (claude-3-5-haiku: 1.00/5.00 there vs 0.80/4.00 in pricing.json, MNT-133), and
  - is SCHEDULED FOR EDITS by P14-4 (bd-6xrq), which moves the Anthropic MD claim 14.7% -> 13.3%.
So the freeze locked the surface that is CORRECT (OpenAI) and left UNFROZEN the surface that is broken and about to change. The freeze as written does not protect the evidence path for tab:xmodel at all.

## How
Either (a) hash-pin _optimizer_glue.py:60-101 as part of the freeze and land P14-4 behind the tag, or (b) reconcile the two tables to one source of truth BEFORE the freeze, then pin that. (b) is better - two disagreeing price tables is itself a defect.

## Success
Every price used to produce a committed cost number is frozen or reconciled. No unfrozen table feeds a published claim.
Findings: MNT-131, MNT-132, MNT-133; red-team A2

title: P14-2-DECISION: guard-scorer fix needs a re-run the freeze defers - AUTHOR CALL
description:
## The conflict (RED-TEAM A4)
P14-2 (fix the empty-string scorer, bd-ardk) is P0 MUST-FIX-BEFORE-SUBMISSION. But correcting the guard delta needs re-scoring against RAW MODEL OUTPUTS, and those are GONE: no traces.db survives, and the per_task.csv sidecars carry only baseline_passed/optimized_passed booleans, computed BY THE BROKEN SCORER. So the corrected guard delta CANNOT be produced from committed data. The freeze pushes the paid re-run post-submission.

## Why it matters
The guard headline is -42.7pp catastrophe to -1.3pp recovery. MNT-135: the scorer passes empty/truncated answers as PASS, and StateDrop's failure mode IS truncation, so part of the recovery is a scoring artifact. Disclosure alone does not fix a headline NUMBER inflated by a scoring bug.

## The decision (author only)
- Option A: re-run the guard evaluation pre-submission under the corrected scorer. PAID, breaks the freeze for this one experiment. analyst_qa is cheap. The honest fix; the guard is the paper centerpiece.
- Option B: ship the guard delta caveated as an upper bound under a containment scorer that admits truncated outputs. Weakens the headline.
- Option C: re-derive a LOWER bound from any raw answers that ARE recoverable.

RECOMMENDATION: Option A. A re-run of one cheap agent to de-risk the centerpiece is worth breaking the freeze for. Do it FIRST, with the corrected scorer AND a pinned model snapshot, and treat its output as canonical.

## Success
The guard delta is produced by a scorer that fails the empty string, OR the paper states the delta is an upper bound.
Findings: MNT-135; red-team A4

title: [Epic] Phase 16: Positioning & Contribution (strategic - reviewer red-team)
description:
## The verdict
A hostile MLSys-reviewer simulation returned WEAK REJECT for the main track, EXPLICITLY assuming every one of the 144 correctness findings is fixed. The concerns are structural - contribution shape, evaluation design, venue fit - and survive any amount of number-fixing. Flips to weak-accept at COLM, clear-accept at a workshop.

## Why the 144 fixes are necessary but NOT sufficient
The whole audit makes the paper CORRECT. It does not make it ACCEPTED. Three structural holes no number-fix touches:
1. INTEGRATION NOVELTY: markets a 9-rule runtime + 'up to 34%' but validates 3 rules in isolation, 2 in composition, on fixtures BUILT TO TRIGGER THEM. The one defensible novel claim is smaller: structure-gated abstention (applies() keys only on universal call properties, never task semantics) as a do-no-harm safety discipline, plus the label-free guard.
2. FIXTURE INVERSION (the deepest hole): four generic agents produced near-zero savings, so fixtures were engineered to activate the rules. On un-engineered traffic the demonstrated behavior is ABSTENTION, not savings. Real-world value is unproven.
3. UNDER-SCALED: n<=300, one real agent, single-trial, no CIs on the headline savings %, <$25 spend, documented 32->100% baseline drift. Systems reviewers steeped in vLLM/Orca will find it integration-heavy and the workloads unconvincing.
Plus the marketing/candor mismatch: honest limitations in the BACK, oversold 9-rule/34% framing in the FRONT - an AC assembles the rejection from the paper's own text.

## The two highest-leverage moves (distinct from bug-fixing)
A. RUN THE RUNTIME BLIND, AT SCALE, ON REAL UN-ENGINEERED AGENT TRAFFIC (a public agentic benchmark - tau-bench / GAIA-agentic / SWE-bench Verified - or real LangChain/AutoGen traces you did NOT construct), let structure-gating decide where rules fire, report aggregate cost+accuracy over MULTIPLE TRIALS with CIs. This is the one experiment that converts 'helps on benchmarks I built for it' into 'helps in the wild' - the exact sentence a meta-reviewer needs to accept. If savings survive: systems paper. If it's mostly abstention: that's the honest ceiling, and it's a workshop paper.
B. DEMOTE the 9-rule/34% framing; RE-CENTER on structure-gated abstention + the divergence guard, so the honest limitations become peripheral instead of load-bearing. Cheap (a rewrite), and it lifts the ceiling.

## Strongest assets to build on (the reviewer credited these)
- The LLMLingua-2 dual-regime head-to-head: genuinely strong, clean, mechanistic, 4-OOM overhead win. The real finding.
- The evaluation METHODOLOGY (shared-baseline ablation, input-token-as-deterministic-attribution, documented failure modes) - the MOST MLSys-native, transferable piece, currently UNDERSOLD relative to the rules.
- The label-free guard as a demonstration (contain -42.7pp with no labels while preserving a benign rule).

## Decision this forces (author, strategic)
The 144-fix plan produces a submission-ready CORRECT paper. Whether that paper goes to MLSys (weak reject as-is), COLM (weak accept), or a workshop (accept) - OR whether to invest in move A (the at-scale blind experiment) to earn MLSys - is a strategic call the plan does not make. Decide venue/scope BEFORE spending 14 weeks on 144 fixes tuned for MLSys.

title: P11-7b: disable CLI silently accepts unknown rule names (latent ablation footgun)
description:
## What
'agentc optimize disable --rule ContxtCompress' (a typo) prints 'Disabled ContxtCompress on 1 call site' and writes the verbatim name. No validation against the known rule set.

## Why (latent, NOT a current defect)
The ablation driver's RULES names all match the runtime exactly (verified), so today's paper ablations are correct. BUT a future typo in bench/optimizer_ablation.py RULES would produce a silent no-op '-off' config: the disable row's rule name never matches a real rule, so the rule keeps firing and the '-off' column measures nothing while looking valid.

## Fix
Validate --rule against the registered rule set in cmd_optimize_disable; reject unknown names.

## Success
A typo'd rule name fails loudly.
Findings: P11-7 diagnostic

title: [GATE] POST-SUBMISSION — do NOT start any dependent until the paper is submitted
description:
## What
A standing gate. Every bead that CHANGES RUNTIME CODE or REGENERATES COMMITTED EVIDENCE depends on this. It stays OPEN until the paper is submitted, so 'br ready' never surfaces behavior-changing work during the submission window.

## Why
The freeze bead (bd-3w1) was a one-shot 'set up the freeze' TASK. Closing it (freeze established) RELEASED its dependents into ready — the opposite of intended. A freeze is a STATE, not a completed task. This gate encodes the state: closed only when submission happens.

## The invariant it protects
Every number in main.tex was produced by the frozen runtime. Changing that runtime means the committed CSVs no longer match the shipped code, and an artifact reviewer who re-runs gets different numbers. So: freeze the runtime, fix the paper + artifact AROUND it, and land all behavior-changing beads AFTER submission (on a post-submission branch).

## When to close
Only after the paper is submitted. Then the gated beads become ready on the post-submission branch.
DO NOT close to 'unblock work' — that defeats the freeze.
close_reason: Retired: built on a submission-imminent assumption that does not hold (submission is far off; goal is repo cleanup). Superseded by specs/working/rerun-ledger.md — the impact review found NO cited experiment needs a paid re-run, so code fixes proceed as normal cleanup with the ledger flagging the 7 beads that touch a committed number.

title: P8-13: Golden planner-ranking-order test — PREREQUISITE for the C3 + driver-consolidation refactors
description:
## What
Add a regression test that asserts the planner's rule-ranking ORDER (which rewrite wins) on fixed inputs, plus a golden-output check on a small committed sample. This must exist BEFORE the two evidence-touching refactors land.

## Why (the grader's #1 risk)
bd-yqr (C1-C5) and bd-n8s (25 drivers -> 1) can silently flip which rewrite the planner selects -> change a committed cost/token number -> and NOTHING currently catches it (no test asserts ranking order). The old freeze quarantined these; retiring the freeze removed that guard without adding this test.

## MNT-145 — THE SPECIFIC HAZARD in C3 (read before touching bd-yqr)
